event.title: US and Australia Halt Consular Services in Brazil Ahead of Presidential Election
event.canonical_title: US and Australia Halt Consular Services in Brazil Ahead of Presidential Election
event.summary: The United States and Australia have suspended their consular services in Brazil due to security concerns, just two days before the presidential election. This decision comes amid a heated campaign between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro.

timeline.title: Brazil Prepares for Presidential Elections Amidst Controversies and Merchandising Craze
timeline.summary: Brazil is gearing up for its presidential elections, with nearly 159 million voters expected to participate. The campaign has seen a surge in merchandise sales for candidates, particularly for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Tensions are high as Lula and his far-right challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro, clash over issues of sovereignty and US influence, while a controversy surrounding the country's patron saint, Our Lady of Aparecida, adds to the atmosphere ahead of the vote.
key_facts: Brazil will hold general elections with nearly 159 million voters.
Candidates include incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.
Merchandise sales for candidates are booming.
Controversy surrounds the role of Our Lady of Aparecida in the election.

timeline.title: Brazilians Begin Voting in Polarized Presidential Election
timeline.summary: Voting has commenced in Brazil's 2026 presidential election, featuring incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The election is marked by a deeply polarized atmosphere, with polls indicating a tight race that may lead to a runoff. Approximately 160 million voters are also selecting lawmakers, senators, and governors in this significant electoral event.
key_facts: Incumbent President Lula da Silva is seeking a fourth nonconsecutive term.
Flávio Bolsonaro is the main challenger and son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.
The election involves nearly 160 million voters choosing various political offices.

timeline.title: Brazil Court Demands Meta Ensure Equal Treatment for Lula and Bolsonaro Campaigns
timeline.summary: Brazil's top electoral court has ordered Meta to demonstrate that it is providing equal treatment to campaign content from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. The court has set a 24-hour deadline for compliance and has threatened a daily fine for failure to adhere to this ruling. This decision follows allegations from Lula's campaign regarding the suppression of his content ahead of the upcoming presidential runoff.
key_facts: Brazil's top electoral court issued a 24-hour order to Meta.
Meta must prove equal treatment of campaign content for Lula and Bolsonaro.

timeline.title: Lula Wins Fourth Term as Brazil's President Amid Controversy
timeline.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a historic fourth term as president of Brazil, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro with 51.79% of the vote in a runoff election. Despite Lula's victory, Flávio Bolsonaro has refused to concede. The opposition party has accepted the election results, while former President Trump has claimed the vote appeared 'rigged,' although no evidence has been provided to support this assertion.
key_facts: Lula won 51.79% of the vote in the runoff election.
Flávio Bolsonaro received 48.21% of the vote.
Bolsonaro's party has accepted the election results.
Flávio Bolsonaro has not conceded defeat.
Trump has called the election 'rigged' without evidence.

event_overview.title: About Brazil Elections
event_overview.subject: Brazil Elections
event_overview.summary: Brazil’s 2026 general election chose the country’s president and vice president alongside governors, senators, and federal and state or district legislators. The presidential contest used a nationwide two-round majoritarian system, with a runoff only if no candidate won an absolute majority of valid first-round votes.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The first round was held nationwide on October 4, 2026; the presidential and gubernatorial runoff, where required, was held on October 25, 2026.

facts.label: Offices and geographic scope
facts.value: These were simultaneous general elections across Brazil for president and vice president, state and Federal District governors and vice governors, senators and their substitutes, and federal, state, and district deputies.

facts.label: Election authority
facts.value: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) administered the 2026 process under Resolution No. 23,751/2026, covering preparation, voting, counting, aggregation of results, certification, and post-election procedures.

facts.label: Presidential voting system
facts.value: A presidential candidate needed more than half of valid votes in the first round to win outright; blank and null votes were excluded. Otherwise, the two leading candidates advanced to a new second-round vote.

facts.label: Term and inauguration
facts.value: The president and vice president serve four-year terms. For the 2026 election, the TSE calendar set inauguration for January 5, 2027.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows a limited set of election-period developments, including consular-service changes, voting, campaign and platform issues, polling, and the reported outcome; it does not aim to be a complete record of Brazil’s electoral administration, all candidates, or every legal and political development.
